abstract: Oversees pathogen disinfection barrier validation, pathogen log reduction credits, and membrane filtration energy metrics
system_message:
You are Process engineering lead (PROC). The process engineering lead oversees the technical evaluation of pathogen disinfection barrier validations, allocated pathogen log-reduction credits across treatment sequences, and baseline electrical power requirements for membrane filtration equipment.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Oversees pathogen disinfection barrier validation, pathogen log reduction credits, and membrane filtration energy metrics（TREAT）
information_points.content:
PROC-TREAT-M1F：For the Engineered wetlands sequential treatment system, regulatory multi-barrier pathogen disinfection validation is confirmed based on a 180-day operational pilot test. Over the complete treatment sequence, the model secures a cumulative regulatory virus log-reduction credit of 12 log, while the continuous baseline membrane filtration power demand for nominal throughput is 780 kW.
PROC-TREAT-1J0：For the Indirect aquifer recharge infiltration basin, regulatory multi-barrier pathogen disinfection validation is confirmed based on a 180-day operational pilot test. Over the complete treatment sequence, the model secures a cumulative regulatory virus log-reduction credit of 10 log, while the continuous baseline membrane filtration power demand for nominal throughput is 780 kW.
PROC-TREAT-08J：For the Direct potable reuse multi-barrier train, regulatory multi-barrier pathogen disinfection validation is confirmed based on a 180-day operational pilot test. Over the complete treatment sequence, the model secures a cumulative regulatory virus log-reduction credit of 12 log, while the continuous baseline membrane filtration power demand for nominal throughput is 620 kW.

information_points.title: Filter backwash recovery（BACKWASH）
information_points.content:
PROC-BACKWASH-DJK：For the Engineered wetlands sequential treatment system, audit data shows a backwash water recovery efficiency of 92% during the daily automated filter backwash recycling cycle.
PROC-BACKWASH-NA9：For the Indirect aquifer recharge infiltration basin, audit data shows a backwash water recovery efficiency of 88% during the daily automated filter backwash recycling cycle.
PROC-BACKWASH-PMP：For the Direct potable reuse multi-barrier train, audit data shows a backwash water recovery efficiency of 96% during the daily automated filter backwash recycling cycle.
